title: Blueberries and Digestive Health: How Fiber Contributes to Your Well-Being
metaDescription: Learn how the fiber in blueberries contributes to normal intestinal transit and satiety, and how to include them in your routine to look after your digestion.
excerpt: Fiber is one of digestion’s great allies, and blueberries are a delicious way to add it to your day.
imageAlt: Breakfast bowl with yogurt, oats, chia seeds and fresh blueberries next to a glass of water

blocks.text: Good digestion starts with what we put on the plate. Dietary fiber, water and minimally processed foods are the foundation, and blueberries provide all three.
What fiber does in your body
Fiber is the part of plants that our body does not fully digest. It contributes to normal intestinal transit, gives a feeling of fullness and feeds the beneficial bacteria in the gut.
A cup of fresh blueberries (about 150 g) provides around 3.6 g of fiber. General recommendations for adults are around 25–30 g a day, and most people do not reach that figure.

items: Blueberries + oats: two sources of fiber in a single breakfast.
Blueberries + plain yogurt or kefir: fiber alongside fermented foods.
Blueberries + chia or flaxseed: a tablespoon of seeds adds even more fiber.

blocks.text: Tips to increase fiber without discomfort

items: Increase fiber gradually, over several weeks.
Drink enough water throughout the day.
Spread fruits and vegetables across several meals instead of concentrating them in one.

blocks.text: If you have a diagnosed digestive condition, consult your doctor or nutritionist before making major changes to your diet.
